article_title: Advancing Family and Community Engagement: A Regional Collaborative
citation: Region 15 Comprehensive Center. (2022). Advancing Family and Community Engagement: A Regional Collaborative. https://region15cc.org
title: The Region 15 FACE Collaborative: a four-state leadership network for state education agency family and community engagement leaders
description: The FACE Collaborative is a regional network established by R15CC in 2022 for SEA leaders in Arizona, California, Nevada, and Utah. Its design was shaped by needs-sensing that found leadership structures for family and community engagement "varied significantly among the four states" and that limited information sharing and coordination impeded progress. The Collaborative provided a space where leaders shared practices, learned from experts, and developed state-level projects.
requirements: Participation of state education agency leaders responsible for family and community engagement across member states
constraints: Designed around needs-sensing findings specific to the four-state region, including varied state leadership structures and limited cross-SEA communication
target_learners: State education agency family and community engagement leaders
target_learning_goals: Designing and implementing family and community engagement practices
examples: Leaders supported each other in building an active practice-centered knowledge base and shared current resources and evidence-based best practices
key_sources: Region 15 Comprehensive Center. (2022). Advancing Family and Community Engagement: A Regional Collaborative. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED651087

article_title: A Comparative Analysis of Institutional and Course Generative AI Policies within Higher Education: Implications for Instruction in Computing Education
citation: Amrita Ganguly, Aditya Johri, Nora McDonald, Areej Ali, Umama Dewan, and Aayushi Hingle Collier. (2026). A Comparative Analysis of Institutional and Course Generative AI Policies within Higher Education: Implications for Instruction in Computing Education.
title: Linked dataset of institutional GenAI policies and CS course syllabi from U.S. R1 universities
description: A linked two-level dataset built from the Carnegie Classification list of 131 R1 institutions. Researchers searched university websites for GenAI policies from October 9 to November 26, 2023; fourteen institutions had no policy or mention of GenAI, leaving 116 institutions in the analysis with 141 documents collected. Course syllabi were collected from March 4 to May 11, 2024 via Google searches for computer science course syllabi, resulting in 98 syllabi from 54 R1 universities, each treated and coded as a separate unit. The overlap analysis found 47 institutions have both institutional and course-level guidelines.
requirements: Publicly available documents only, collected under Institutional Review Board approval
constraints: Restricted to U.S. R1 institutions and CS syllabi, limiting generalizability to other institution types and disciplines; does not capture how policies are implemented, interpreted, or enforced in practice
target_learners: Higher education instructors and administrators in computing education
target_learning_goals: Understanding alignment between institutional and course-level GenAI guidance
examples: Figure 1 shows among 131 R1 institutes how many have institutional guidelines (116), course level guidelines (54) and both (47)
key_sources: Amrita Ganguly, Aditya Johri, Nora McDonald, Areej Ali, Umama Dewan, and Aayushi Hingle Collier. (2026). A Comparative Analysis of Institutional and Course Generative AI Policies within Higher Education: Implications for Instruction in Computing Education. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12296
